text:
zoe: Heads-up: our examples smoke started failing after the latest typegen publish. runtime shows missing client defaults in browser bundles.
ali: can you paste the CI snippet?
zoe: short stack:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'retries')
  at new ApiClient (dist/sdk/api.js:78:18)
```
frank: I grabbed the regen diff 1 files changed7. There's an internal refactor that moves default options into a top-level init function and also reorders a couple exports.
ali: did the release note mention semver impact?
build-bot: published @redwood/typegen@1.2.0 at 1877998000. changelog: "refactor(core): move defaults to init; perf: export reorder". No semver line present.
tara: reordering exports + moving init into a separate side-effect means some bundlers can drop the init if import order changes. That's exactly what esbuild did for our example app.
zoe: immediate mitigation 1) pin typegen in examples to 1.1.3 and re-run CI, 2) open a rollback PR for the generator to restore previous init behavior.
frank: agree. longer term: release workflow needs a post-publish validation step that runs `yarn install --frozen-lockfile && yarn build` for canonical examples and checks for runtime sanities.
ali: also add a mandatory "Semver-Impact" line in changelogs. if defaults or runtime behavior changes, it should be at least a minor and flagged.
tara: additional suggestion: publish potentially-breaking refactors under npm tag "staging"/"next" so caret ranges don't upgrade consumers unexpectedly.
build-bot: noted: follow-up tasks created: #634 (rollback generator), #635 (postpublish example builds), #636 (enforce changelog semver line), #637 (publish-tagging policy).
zoe: PR to pin examples opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/912 127. CI queued.
ali: once rollback lands we should run a diff test and then republish with clear semver. thanks team.
frank: adding a tiny bundler test to our typegen CI that uses both webpack and esbuild to catch ordering-sensitive breaks.
zoe: CI green after pin. closing thread but tracking in #634.
